_doc: How a work that does not fit the Void tower is made to fit (Palle, 2026-11-09: 'we can build a catalog of strategies that make it easier to fit the work ... In the end it is about conveying an idea'). AUTHORED: strategies are edited by hand; cases are appended by tools/void_fit.py record after each work is fitted and re-measured (tools/void_size_survey.py). A placement that uses a strategy carries config.fit {strategies: [...], strip, strip_parts, keep_parts, set, note} - the tower records what was done, this file what was learned.

strategies.name: Move it on its own floor
strategies.when: Its footprint fits the slab (42 x 18 m) and its height the storey, it just stands past an edge or over nothing.
strategies.how: python tools/void_fit_pass.py (nearest free spot: on the slab or a side slab, off the shafts, round no column, clear of every other work); edit position.
strategies.cost: Order and route are not in the search; check the floor's arrangement (/api/spine-roles).
strategies.learned: 2026-11-09 ML + shaders: 27 of 28 fitted by a move alone or after another strategy. Run the fit pass AFTER strip/raise/scale (sizes change), and per floor in sequence - the first version put two works on one spot. Isosurfaces + soft bodies: 45 of 45 - nine chapter consoles stood 3-5 m past the south edge; a quarter turn put each on the edge band. L-systems + boolean surfaces: 30 of 30. THE SURVEY JUDGES EACH WORK ALONE: two works standing in each other, or a tower column through a work, both read 'fits' - after pass A, 22 such pairs stood on these 11 floors, most from works SCALED where they stood (a scale keeps the box centre, and a smaller box can land astride a column row). `void_fit.py overlaps <decisions>` lists them and `void_fit_pass.py --overlaps` moves them (the one round a column, else the smaller of the pair). Run both after every pass. Two fit-pass faults found on the way: it read a side slab's measured box as deck, but the box holds the tangled beams, whose feet spread 1 m past the deck's ends (a work 0.4 m off the slab's end read as on it); and it kept its edge margin on a north slab's INNER edge, leaving a 27 cm strip of no ground just inside the edge. Both read the deck from the placement now (void_size_survey.slab_decks / slab_grounds). Overlap pass (2026-11-09, 68 floors re-measured): the five pairs fitted before the check carried 121 overlaps - 99 a column through a work. 42 cleared by a move alone (fit pass --overlaps, holding other sessions' uncommitted works with --hold). The open middle between the shafts (x +-7, z +-6.5) is the one place on a floor for a work up to 14 x 13 m: give it to the floor's walk-in hero. A box is not a body: two flags were markers, not size - a VR brush resting 15 m from its 2 m sculpting volume, and a probe drawn through the work it tests. Read the parts before moving the whole. The fit pass cannot see a gallery laid on a slab (it reads as an extension): check it by hand.

strategies.name: A quarter turn
strategies.when: A long work fits along the floor but not across it.
strategies.how: facing +90 (the fit pass tries it).
strategies.learned: 8 of 8: long works (a row of panels, a line of bodies) fit along the floor's 42 m.

strategies.name: Remove its own floor
strategies.says: Many works have a floor and walls of their own and they have to be removed.
strategies.when: The work brings a ground plane, grid or stage floor bigger than what it shows.
strategies.how: config.fit.strip: ["floor"] (flat, at the base, >= 25 % of the work) or strip_parts by name.
strategies.cost: Bodies that rolled or walked on its floor now use the tower slab: inside the building only.
strategies.learned: 11 of 11 where the floor was a plain ground plane, grid or stage (ML: 40 m creature ground, 48 m grid, 12 m planes). On shader rooms it did little: their floors wear the shader and are kept - those need a surface, i.e. the playground setup.

strategies.name: Remove its own walls
strategies.when: Backdrops, room walls, frames around the idea.
strategies.how: config.fit.strip: ["walls"] (upright, thin, on its perimeter).
strategies.cost: If a wall is needed, use tower_walls or the playground.
strategies.learned: 6 of 6, but the shader parlour and pattern rooms barely shrank: their walls are the shader too.

strategies.name: Remove its own ceiling
strategies.when: A lid or canopy that pushes it through the slab above.
strategies.how: config.fit.strip: ["ceiling"].

strategies.name: Tower elements as walls
strategies.says: In many cases if a wall is needed we can use tower elements or the playground.
strategies.when: The idea needs a wall, a backdrop or a corner after its own were stripped.
strategies.how: The floor's construction cells (cube, deck, truss, wedge) in /lab-editor, or the building's columns and edge.

strategies.name: Fit it into a playground setup
strategies.says: the shader should be fit into playground setups
strategies.when: Shader and material works: a few receivers with a material, sliders, a label, inside a stage or parlour.
strategies.how: A board with "wear": <the shader work on the floor> - its plates wear the work's live materials (by shader, or wear_index); tools/shader_gallery.py place writes a floor's gallery from its console. Strip the stage around it first.
strategies.cost: The scaffold playground system is not committed yet (2026-11-09).
strategies.learned: 2026-11-09: all six shader floors have a gallery of walkable screens wearing their console (tools/test_shader_gallery_tower.py 6/6); the composition stage stands on boards wearing its own material - the surround IS the material. A chapter console builds one mode at a time: the other screens show their own copy until it switches.

strategies.name: A side slab, at most 10 m out
strategies.says: We can have an extra slab on the side but then I do not want that to be more than like ten meters out and then I want tangled support beams to the floor under. We can let the slab contract and expand, 10 meters per floor.
strategies.when: A work or a field that needs more depth than 18 m, or room beside a full floor.
strategies.how: Place void_slab_extension on the building edge facing out: config length (2-42), depth (1-10).
strategies.cost: It reads as architecture: use it where the idea needs the room.
strategies.learned: 6 works stand on 4 slabs (ML_Evolution south 16 x 8; Shader_05 north 39 x 8; Shader_11 north 16 x 5; Shader_12 north 30 x 6): rooms 4-7 m past the north edge of a full floor. A slab must span the whole overhang along the edge, not just most of it. Procedural generation + swarm: six works that are walked at body scale (three walkable fitness landscapes, a crowd walk, a maze, a drone comparison) stood 3-6 m past one edge of a floor with no free centre: one slab each, as long as the work and its overhang plus a metre deep - all fit. Forces: VFM_05_Launch got slabs on both sides (40 x 7), VFM_03_Motion one south for three 10 m plays, the fields floor both sides, Change_Choreography one north for the conveyor. L-systems + boolean surfaces: the tower's columns stand on two rows, z = +-7, at x = +-5, +-14, +-20 (at most 10 m apart), so a work wider than 10 m can never cross a column row: inside the building it must stay within z +-6.5 (13 m, minus the shafts at x +-10), and anything deeper stands on a slab, where the deck plus the edge strip to the column row gives 11.5 m at a 10 m slab. Boolean_Works (13 works, two walk-in bays of 12.7 and 16.7 m) took both: north 26 x 10 (burrow, SDF cavern, eggs), south 22 x 10 (the Kapoor bay, its inner edge 5 cm past the column row, turned so its console faces the floor). Keep a work off the slab's side rails: they are the deck's ends. Overlap pass over the five earlier pairs: the commonest fault was a work half on a slab and half in the building, astride a column row - fitted at the edge, never at the row. Twelve slabs were deepened (to 8-10 m) so each such work stands WHOLLY past the row, its inner edge 5 cm off it; two slabs went, empty once their walks moved into the open middle. Rule: a slab work's inner edge sits at |z| >= 7.45.

strategies.name: Raise it onto the slab
strategies.when: It was built on a museum stage: its parts sit below its origin and go down through the slab (and bodies fall).
strategies.how: placement height = the depth it reaches below the slab.
strategies.cost: None when its top still fits.
strategies.learned: 9 of 11: museum stage works build below their origin (2-3 m); in the tower they sat under the slab and their bodies fell for hundreds of metres. Raise by the depth the survey reports. Two then hit the ceiling: raise + scale. Isosurfaces + soft bodies: 20 of 20, computed from the measured depth (height += depth). A work too tall by less than the slab's 0.36 m may sink that much into the slab instead (the rhizome body, which ignores its placement scale).

strategies.name: Scale an area work
strategies.says: Sometimes it can work to scale the area artifact.
strategies.when: Fields, landscapes, diagrams - works looked at or walked round, not walked through at body scale.
strategies.how: placement scale.
strategies.cost: Never for works whose lesson is the body's size (passages, Drink Me, approach works).
strategies.learned: 7 of 9: fields and water surfaces (creature field 0.35, basin 0.62); a small step (0.92) clears a ceiling. Isosurfaces: landscapes and fields 0.025-0.42 (11 of 11). Watch body-scale meaning: the gyroid at 0.13 keeps its probe but its passages are now below body size - the probe honestly reports them closed. Not for works with bodies inside scaled colliders: the random-walk cave was reverted to full size (taller-floor case). L-systems: trees, curves and cities are looked at, not walked: the 19.5 m Modulor cypress 0.28, the 22.7 m tube tree 0.24, the 22 m city 0.25, the 15 m Hilbert curve 0.35 (those four want a shaft or a taller floor if the height is the point). A scale keeps the work's centre: eight of the scaled works then stood round a tower column - run the overlap check after a scale, not only after a move. Application bays (the cone of 'One cut, three rooms') are walked: 0.68 is the smallest kept, chosen to fit the open middle between the shafts. Swarm walks (12-14.4 m) went into the open middle turned and at 0.93-0.95; long galleries and tunnels (18-19 m) to 0.49-0.95 so they fit the 3.5 m strip between a shaft and a column row. A physics play (the wind room) took 0.91 with its floor plate stripped, the least that fits a 10 m slab.

strategies.name: Fewer of the same element
strategies.says: sometimes we can reduce the artifact if it consists of many of the same element.
strategies.when: Layers, feature maps, rows, copies: the idea survives with fewer.
strategies.how: config.fit.set: the work's own exported count (num_layers, feature_map_count, grid_size, ...).
strategies.cost: Check the count still carries the idea (three of a kind still reads as a series; one does not).
strategies.learned: 4 of 4 once the right setting was found: read the script that is actually placed (the CNN's VR script has num_filters_per_layer, not feature_map_count; the first try was refused and reported). Typed arrays are rebuilt by fit.set. A work that builds part of itself on its PARENT (force_mower's lawn) ignores placement scale: use its own size settings (lawn_width, lawn_length) - read the code, the registry often says where. The work's own size, not its scale, where it has one: the mower's lawn_length 14 -> 12.4 lands it between the column rows; the boid flock's boid_boundary 16 x 14 -> 10.5 x 10.5. A flock overshoots its bounds by a spring's swing, max_speed / sqrt(force / margin): set boid_boundary_force (new, opt-in) rather than shrinking the box further.

strategies.name: Distribute it across the floor
strategies.says: sometimes we might be able to convey the meaning of the artifact by distributing across the floor in another way.
strategies.when: A work made of separable stations or panels that stood together in a hall.
strategies.how: Several placements of its parts, or the floor's own route through them.

strategies.name: Rise through a shaft
strategies.when: Too tall for the storey: stand it under a shaft opening so it rises into the floor above (the tower already does this).
strategies.how: Position over shaft A or B on a floor whose shaft is open above.
strategies.cost: The floor above must keep the opening clear.

strategies.name: A taller floor
strategies.when: Several tall works on one floor.
strategies.how: python tools/insert_void_floor.py --storey 12 for a new floor; an existing floor's storey is a levels edit.
strategies.cost: Every floor below drops; floor numbers do not change.

strategies.name: A floor of its own
strategies.when: A space bigger than a floor (atria, landscapes, arenas): a room in its own right.
strategies.how: tools/insert_void_floor.py; or an exterior extension like Drink Me.

strategies.name: A portal
strategies.says: Later in the spine we can use Godot's 3D portal.
strategies.when: Later sequences: a space elsewhere, seen and entered through an opening.
strategies.how: Not built yet.

strategies.name: Fix the work
strategies.when: It is drawn far from its floor or its bodies fly off: world-coordinate meshes, physics blow-ups.
strategies.how: Read its code.
strategies.learned: joint_learn_walk reset its walker to world (0,1,0) - the top of the tower - and flew apart: its own frame now. neural_networks_vr still drops something ~495 m: open. The gyroid console's 12 m probe was fixed to the gyroid's museum scale: it now scales with it. rounded_softbody_test blows up only on some runs (876 m): open. boid_manager: its boids' boundary was a box round the world origin (the tower's top); the manager now gives them its own frame, and an opt-in boid_boundary (with a firmer steer) keeps a flock on one floor. Physics that misbehaves on some runs only (caverandomwalk 828 m, rhizomatic_maze_space 80-90 m) is not caused by the fit: reverting the scale or height did not stop it. Compile-check every touched script - a typed-inference error once shipped (6f48ba100). The gyroid console: its probe scaled, but the rail drawn along it was a fixed 12 m in the console's own frame, so turning the console swung a 12 m bar sideways; the rail now lies along the world probe at the probe's length, and the readout says the real length. A fix that makes a work BUILD can make it overflow: measure again after any parse fix.

strategies.name: Keep one
strategies.when: The same work stands on two floors of the same sequence.
strategies.how: Remove the second placement; say why.
strategies.cost: Check which floor's idea it carries.
strategies.learned: The evolved creatures stood on ML_Evolution and ML_Gradient_Landscape: kept on Evolution.

strategies.name: Keep the idea, not the museum's furniture
strategies.when: Museum wayfinding and hall furniture that only works in the museum: teleport lecterns, hall signs, entrance walls.
strategies.how: Remove the placement; move its timeline row (often already on the environment track) to removed, with the reason.
strategies.learned: 2026-11-09 forces: ten force_hall lecterns (teleport to the museum's previous / next hall) stood 5 m past the south edge of ten floors; all removed.

strategies.name: Kept where it stands, on purpose
strategies.when: The overlap is the work: a body bigger than a column bay, a probe drawn through the work it tests.
strategies.how: config.fit.strategies gets "kept", config.fit.note says why; void_fit.py overlaps and void_fit_pass.py --overlaps leave it out.
strategies.cost: An honest exception, visible in the tower's own data; each one is a candidate for a better answer (its own floor, a code change).
strategies.learned: 2026-11-09: rhizome_inside (24 x 25 m, a body walked inside, already at its smallest walkable size, four columns in its bounds); the gyroid console (its probe crosses the gyroid by design).
